solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Small group running riot

indicators.note: running here means run riot, out of order, so the four letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A little band of people is out on the streets causing a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running riot' reads as one idiom, but 'running' is the anagram signal working on RIOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of three performers or people is a small group by definition.

clue.text: Endangered creature Greek character's keeping at home

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so the Greek letter surrounds the next piece

parts.note: rho is a letter of the Greek alphabet
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A Greek man keeps an endangered animal in his house.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhinoceros is a large animal many of whose species are threatened with extinction.

clue.text: Process of arranging gold treasury share

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
a treasure chest holds treasure, so a chest is a treasury
a ration is an allotted share

explanation.surface: Planning how the gold in the treasury is to be divided up.
explanation.definitionFit: Arranging music for an orchestra is called orchestration; more widely it means organising something.

clue.text: Begin introducing law that's upset faithful

indicators.note: introducing means bringing something into the start word, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to begin is to start

indicators.note: upset means knocked about, so the letters of law are jumbled

explanation.surface: Bringing in a law that annoys the loyal members of a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Begin' reads as an instruction to start the clue, but it is the outer word, and 'upset' scrambles the law it takes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalwart is a loyal, dependable supporter, so the adjective is a synonym of faithful.

clue.text: Small flat playing card?

parts.note: a flat surface is even

explanation.surface: A little flat piece of card used in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the cards in a pack is the seven, so this is an example signalled by the question mark.

clue.text: Cooking nearly all tropical fruit

indicators.note: cooking means something is being prepared or cooked up, so letters are mixed
nearly all means the word tropical loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Cooking almost every kind of tropical fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly all' drops the L of TROPICAL, and 'Cooking' rearranges TROPICA.
explanation.definitionFit: An apricot is a small orange stone fruit, so this is an example of a fruit.

clue.text: Source of oil quietly set aside is still looking good

parts.note: an oil well is where oil comes from
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
something set aside is reserved

explanation.surface: An oil well quietly put aside still looks in good shape.
explanation.definitionFit: An older person or thing in good condition for its age is described with this idiom.

clue.text: Rose Walker

definitions.meaning: a climbing rose variety, a kind of flower
a person who hikes in the countryside for pleasure

explanation.surface: A person named Rose Walker.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names both a climbing rose and someone who walks in the country for pleasure.

clue.text: Find record has finished

parts.note: a gramophone record is a disc
when something has finished it is over

explanation.surface: Someone tracks down a record only to learn it has ended.
explanation.definitionFit: To discover something is to find it, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Severely hit British meat

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or beat hard

explanation.surface: A cut of British meat has taken a heavy blow, perhaps from prices.
explanation.definitionFit: The flesh of a young sheep is eaten as a meat.

clue.text: New reverend returning to run what ministers do

parts.note: to run, as an engine runs, is to go

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the letters for New reverend are read backwards

parts.note: Rev is the abbreviation of the title reverend

explanation.surface: A newly ordained clergyman comes back to take on what ministers of religion do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ministers' suggests clergy, matching 'reverend', but here it means government ministers; the 'to run' piece goes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Government ministers rule the country, which is to govern it.

clue.text: Reversed slump in American petrol

indicators.note: Reversed means the word for slump is read from the end

parts.note: to sag is to slump

explanation.surface: A reversal of the slump in American fuel prices.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call petrol gasoline, shortened to gas.

clue.text: Copper on front of short polar dome

indicators.note: on front of places the copper symbol before the next piece

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: short means the word polar loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A copper-clad dome sits on the front of a stubby polar building.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupola is a small rounded dome on a roof, so this is a synonym.

clue.text: Frequently in condition, organ is the latest in technology

parts.note: a condition, as in a state of repair, is a state
oft is an old word for frequently
the heart is a bodily organ

explanation.surface: An organ that is often in good condition counts as the latest technology.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes whatever is the most advanced level currently reached, as in modern gadgets.

clue.text: Row about slip showing dog chasing foxes

indicators.note: about means around, so the row word goes round the other piece

parts.note: a tier is a row of seats
to slip up is to err

explanation.surface: An argument over a mistake involving a hunting dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like an argument, but here it is a line, a tier.
explanation.definitionFit: Terriers were bred to go to earth after foxes and other burrowing animals.

clue.text: Remote camp for soldier not in mail

parts.note: someone not in is out
the British post is mail

explanation.surface: A soldier at a far-off camp has no letters arriving.
explanation.definitionFit: An outpost is a small military station far from the main force.

clue.text: Deserter's returning as sailor

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the deserter word is read backwards

parts.note: a rat is someone who deserts a cause; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A deserter comes back as a seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: Tar is an old informal name for a sailor, a crossword favourite.

clue.text: Part of turkey baster is broken

indicators.note: is broken means the word baster is smashed and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: While roasting a turkey, the cook's baster has broken.
explanation.definitionFit: The breast is the white-meat portion of a roast bird, so it is one part of it.

clue.text: Ingenious key comes with operating handle

parts.note: C is a musical key
a lever is a handle used to operate machinery

explanation.surface: A smart key that comes with a handle for working a lock.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever and ingenious are synonyms for showing inventive skill.

clue.text: Some tobacco licensing is a pain

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Getting a licence to sell tobacco is a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: Colic is a severe abdominal pain, so the definition with its verb gives the noun's meaning.

clue.text: Wear down Queen with celebratory poem

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
an ode is a lyric poem praising something

explanation.surface: Wearing down the Queen with a poem in her honour.
explanation.definitionFit: To erode is to wear something away gradually, a synonym.

clue.text: Bird inside of skip found by waif, oddly

indicators.note: the inside of a word is its letters without the two ends
oddly means take the first, third and so on letters of waif

explanation.surface: A bird is discovered by a homeless child inside a builder's skip.
explanation.walkthrough: A British skip is a large open container for builders' rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: The kiwi is a flightless New Zealand bird, so this is an example of the category.

clue.text: Forgetfulness leads to our best violin being shattered

indicators.note: the leads of words are their opening letters, here of our and best
being shattered means the instrument word is broken up and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Forgetting things results in our finest violin getting smashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads to' looks like 'results in', but it takes the opening letters of 'our' and 'best'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblivion is the state of being unaware or having forgotten, close to forgetfulness.

clue.text: De Gaulle's language mostly about English — it turned wild

indicators.note: about means going round, so the shortened language name surrounds the other letters
mostly means nearly all, so the language name loses its final letter

parts.note: Charles de Gaulle, the French president, spoke French

indicators.note: turned means the word it is flipped round

explanation.surface: De Gaulle's language mostly concerns English, and it became furious.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles de Gaulle was the French wartime leader and president; 'about' wraps the shortened language name round the English letter and the turned word.
explanation.definitionFit: Frenetic means frantic and uncontrolled, close to wild in its sense of frenzied.

clue.text: Reportedly expensive source of venison

indicators.note: Reportedly means as it is said, so the word for expensive is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: something expensive is dear

explanation.surface: Venison is said to be costly meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Venison is the meat of the animal, so the animal is where it comes from.
